rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a heat treatment to vary short-range order, whereas the paper studied as-cast/homogenized single crystals of different compositions without SRO manipulation; both involve controlled comparisons, but the specific lever (SRO vs. composition) differs.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies mechanical loading at ambient to moderately elevated temperatures to avoid diffusion, while the paper covers a wide temperature range (9–1373 K) including cryogenic and high-temperature regimes where diffusion and inertia are active; only the ambient-temperature regime overlaps broadly.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes SRO-induced fault-energy fluctuations pinning dislocations and promoting twinning, whereas the paper's mechanism is solid-solution strengthening via lattice distortion (MSAD), inertial dulling, and Cottrell-type dynamic strain aging; these are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased yield strength and twin density from SRO, while the paper predicts and measures CRSS changes with temperature and composition due to MSAD, inertia, and PLC effects; the predicted property (yield strength increase) is in the same general direction but the underlying cause and specific outcomes differ.
